subject: Renewal health diagnostics + staggered capacity offer
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal health diagnostics + initial observations

Alex — attaching a short runbook and a usage summary we pulled for Q1. High level observations: 
- Token mix shifted ~18% toward generative responses after the February model swap (more long-form responses).
- Median 95th latency is within SLA but we did see a 13% tail increase during peak inference windows (11–13:00 PT).
- Cache hit rate on repeated prompts is ~62%; there's room for prefix caching improvement.

Attachment: clearwave_usage_q1_summary.pdf (PDF)

Suggested next steps: can we schedule a 30-min ops review next week to walk the numbers and discuss a staggered capacity path (pilot burst + reserved trunk)? I sketched two options in the attached spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Diego
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwave.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@clearwave.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health diagnostics + initial observations

Thanks Diego — quick read looks useful. A couple of immediate Qs before we sync: 
1) The latency tail — are those requests primarily coming from our nightly batch scoring or from real-time API calls?
2) The token mix shift — is that a result of a change on our side (prompt templates) or an OCI model behavior?

We can do a 30-min slot Tue 10:00 PT. Priya will join from engineering. Also, can you include cost delta for the staggered path vs a single reserve?

— Alex
Engineering Lead, ClearWave Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwave.com>, Priya Rao <priya@clearwave.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health diagnostics + initial observations

On Tue, Apr 20, 2026 at 8:03 AM Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwave.com> wrote:
> Thanks Diego — quick read looks useful. A couple of immediate Qs before we sync:
> 1) The latency tail — are those requests primarily coming from our nightly batch scoring or from real-time API calls?
> 2) The token mix shift — is that a result of a change on our side (prompt templates) or an OCI model behavior?

Alex/Priya — quick answers from our ops + product side: 
- Tail latency: ~72% of the tail samples correlate to real-time requests during the 11–13 window (customer-facing queries). Nightly batch accounts for 18% of the spike because it overlaps with a refresh job we observed (can be shifted).
- Token mix: early signal shows two things: 1) a prompt template change increased max_tokens in some endpoints; 2) model output length grew slightly after you moved to the new v2.1 model variant. We can provide per-endpoint breakdown during the sync.

Proposal summary (short):
- Pilot: 2-week burst pool (dedicated burst capacity) to absorb peak real-time traffic while we tune caching — includes a one-time setup and a small pilot discount.
- Staggered reserved plan: lower base reserved capacity with a higher burst allowance and pre-agreed short-notice addons. This reduces monthly commit while preserving SLA.

Attachment: staggered-capacity-proposal.xlsx (Excel)

Diego — happy to walk through the worksheet in the call and show the cost delta vs a single full-reserve.

Thanks,
Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Rao <priya@clearwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwave.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 12:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal health diagnostics + initial observations

Ben — appreciate the clarity. Two operational asks before we commit to a pilot: 
- Can Redwood provide a short runbook for shifting the nightly batch window and the expected delta in burst usage if we shift to 03:00 PT?
- For the pilot, what monitoring hooks will we get (metrics/alerts) and can we trial a one-week canary before the two-week burst?

If you can include those two items in the updated spreadsheet and the HubSpot deal, we can speed internal approval. We are targeting a decision by May 5 to align with our Q3 planning.

— Priya
Sr. Platform Engineer, ClearWave Health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Renewal health diagnostics + initial observations

Alex/Priya — noted, and thanks for the timeline. Action items I will own before EOD Friday: 
1) Add a one-week canary option and a sample monitoring hook list to the staggered-capacity-proposal.xlsx.
2) Draft a short runbook for moving your nightly batch to 03:00 PT and estimate the burst delta (we expect a 9–12% lower afternoon tail if batch moves).
3) Push the updated numbers and a one-page executive summary into the HubSpot deal (DEAL-19843) so your procurement team can consume it.

I'll loop Laura for any contract language adjustments if we end up adding a pilot amendment. Thanks — see you on the call.

Best,
Diego
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
